newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air Afrique says Marseille fish imports up 18.5pct.
newsitem.headline: Air Afrique says Marseille fish imports up 18.5pct.

text.p: Pan-African airline, Air Afrique said the volume of fish imports it handled at Marseille-Provence airport in August was up 18.5 percent on August 1995.
Air Afrique operates scheduled Boeing 707 freighter services between Marseille and a number of West African states.
The growth in fish imports last month, mostly from Senegal and Mauritania, was due to strong demand from holiday resorts in southern France, a Marseille-based Air Afrique cargo official told Reuters.

"In the first eight months of the year, we shipped 1,000 tonnes of fish through Marseille compared to 1,100 tonnes for the whole of 1995 so we are confident we can exceed last year's volume before the end of 1996."

Air Afrique's cargo throughput last month was also boosted by the airline's decision to make less belly-hold capacity available for freight on its Airbus 310 and 300 passenger services from Paris to West Africa during the summer months because of high passenger load factors, the official added.
"Some of the freight that would normally have been transported to and from Paris in the bellyholds of Airbuses was handled at Marseille instead," the official added.

Air Afrique currently operates three weekly 707F sevices from Marseille and one weekly 707F service from Paris to West Africa, a programme which will remain unchanged with the introduction of winter schedules at the end of next month, the official said.

"We are likely to continue with normal practice and add extra 707Fs during the green bean harvest in Burkina Faso between December and April," he added - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
